Android 10 needs a computer: connect the phone by USB, run “adb tcpip 5555”, type 5555 here and accept the authorization on the phone.

1. Connect the phone to a Wi‑Fi network.
2. In Settings → About phone, tap “Build number” 7 times to turn on Developer options.
3. In Developer options, turn on “Wireless debugging” and allow the network.
4. So that Android doesn't forget the authorization, also turn on “Disable adb authorization timeout”.
5. On Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO, also turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)”: without it Motocom can't turn wireless debugging on by itself.

This way split screen isn't needed.
1. Tap Pair: Developer options open.
2. Go into Wireless debugging and tap “Pair device with pairing code”.
3. Without closing that dialog, pull down the notification shade and tap “Enter code” on Motocom's notification. If you don't see it, expand the notification with its arrow.
4. Type the 6 digits and send. Motocom finds the ports by itself and starts ADB.

• Open Motocom, then Settings → Developer options → Wireless debugging. Don't open the code yet.
• Open Recents: with gestures, swipe up from the bottom to the middle and hold for a moment; with buttons, tap the square.
• On Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO, long-press Motocom's card and tap “Split screen”. On other phones, tap Motocom's icon above its card.
• Pick Settings as the second app and open “Pair device with pairing code” in that half.
• Drag the middle bar if you need more room. To leave, drag it to an edge.
If your phone can't split the screen, try a floating window.

Just tap Connect: Motocom finds the port by itself and, if Android allows it, turns wireless debugging on and off on its own (on Xiaomi also turn on “USB debugging (Security settings)”). If it can\'t turn it on, turn it on yourself before tapping. You only need to pair again if Android has forgotten the authorization.\n\nAndroid 10 needs a computer; on Android 13 or later the image keeps going with the phone locked.

• Fully close Carbit Ride and OffNavigator before tapping Connect: they use the same ports and only one app can have them.
• Keep Wi‑Fi and location on.
• With the bike stopped, lock the phone and check that the image stays on the bike's screen.
• To enter a destination, tap “To the phone” and then “To the bike”.

If ADB was already on, nothing is needed: it keeps running until you restart the phone, even if Android closes Motocom. If the phone has restarted, use the bike's Wi‑Fi:
• Switch the bike on and open the phone connection on its screen.
• Scan the QR on the bike's screen with Motocom (no ADB needed). Then tap the Bike row on the home screen: “Wi‑Fi” shows the name of the bike's network and “Password”, its password.
• In the phone's Wi‑Fi settings, connect to that network with that password. If it warns there is no internet, stay connected.
• In Motocom tap Start ADB and wait until it says ADB on. If Android asks whether to allow debugging on that network, accept.
• Important: go back to the Wi‑Fi settings and forget that network. Otherwise the bike's screen won't connect.
• Go back to Motocom and tap Connect.
